response.sql:
WITH trans_avgs AS (
  SELECT transref, AVG(anlycount) as trans_avg
  FROM sentimentandfundamentals
  WHERE anlycount IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY transref
),
overall_avg_cte AS (
  SELECT AVG(trans_avg) as overall_avg
  FROM trans_avgs
),
kept_trans AS (
  SELECT ta.transref, ta.trans_avg
  FROM trans_avgs ta, overall_avg_cte oa
  WHERE ta.trans_avg > oa.overall_avg
),
kept_avg_cte AS (
  SELECT AVG(trans_avg) as kept_avg
  FROM kept_trans
),
results AS (
  SELECT 
    kt.transref,
    kt.trans_avg,
    kt.trans_avg - oa.overall_avg as above_overall,
    kt.trans_avg - ka.kept_avg as above_kept
  FROM kept_trans kt, overall_avg_cte oa, kept_avg_cte ka
),
with_rn AS (
  SELECT 
    transref, trans_avg, above_overall, above_kept,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY above_kept DESC NULLS LAST) as rn
  FROM results
)
SELECT transref, trans_avg, above_overall, above_kept
FROM with_rn
WHERE rn <= 10
   OR above_kept = (SELECT above_kept FROM with_rn WHERE rn = 10)
ORDER BY above_kept DESC NULLS LAST

assumptions.assumption: Multiple sentimentandfundamentals records can reference the same transref; per-transaction average is computed by averaging anlycount across all such records (NULLs excluded from average).
"Kept transactions" are those whose per-transaction average exceeds the overall mean of all per-transaction averages (strict inequality: >).
SQLite supports window functions (ROW_NUMBER) and NULLS LAST in ORDER BY (SQLite 3.30+). If not available, the window function can be replaced with a simpler LIMIT/OFFSET subquery pattern.

alternatives.interpretation: "Kept transactions" are those whose average is >= overall average (inclusive) rather than strictly >. This would include transactions exactly at the overall mean.
